items.label: Constellation Energy Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: LONG-TERM NUCLEAR CONTRACTING RESTARTED: ~920 MW of long-term

set.signal: LONG-TERM NUCLEAR CONTRACTING RESTARTED: ~920 MW of long-term nuclear deals signed since the last call, at an AVERAGE DURATION OF 18.5 YEARS, all with INVESTMENT-GRADE customers, priced 'consistent with our view of long-term value' (CFO Shane Smith: 'we have executed nearly 1 GW of nuclear PPAs within the range contemplated by this view' of the March sensitivities, and on pricing 'we're going to keep that range as it is'). Roughly 30% OF CLEAN BASELOAD OUTPUT IS NOW UNDER LONG-TERM AGREEMENT, with the pipeline called 'robust and active'. Counterparties are not disclosed at customer request; the one named deal is WALMART - Walmart's FIRST nuclear PPA and the first such transaction by a major retailer. Dan Eggers: 'Those are signed contracts' and 'these deals are not dependent upon those outcomes' of the pending FERC/PJM decisions. Because the new agreements have later start dates they are not expected to materially affect 2029 earnings, but they extend visibility on base-earnings growth

items.reason: The $20-$50/MWh range was stated by the analyst (Steve Fleishman), not by management; the CFO only said the range is kept as is. The signed-contracts point was Dan Eggers'.
items.evidence: Steve Fleishman: ... I think it's $20-$50 a megawatt hour. ... Shane Smith: ... we're going to keep that range as it is.

items.label: Constellation Energy Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: THE STRANDED-CAPACITY THESIS, restated as the core

set.signal: THE STRANDED-CAPACITY THESIS, restated as the core commercial argument: the grid has unused generation and wires capacity in OVER 99% OF THE HOURS of the year - 'we have a peak capacity concern, not an energy concern' - so the fastest and cheapest path to powering AI is harvesting that latent capacity and managing the handful of peak hours with batteries, demand response, peaking resources and customer backup generation. Management argues existing and new supply are not bifurcated: even a customer that self-manages peaks via Connect and Manage 'will still need to buy energy for all of the other hours', which is where the existing fixed-price, carbon-free nuclear fleet becomes the multi-decade product customers want. Customer sophistication about the grid is now 'as good as the energy companies themselves' - not true two years ago. CEO Joe Dominguez: 'I think what we'll see is very shortly, the entirety of the data economy investing what could be upwards of $1 trillion in infrastructure annually when you put all the pieces together', and 'I believe that once we do get clarity, we're going to see here in PJM what we've seen in many places where deal flow will kick off with a bit of a bang.'
set.figure: grid unused >99% of hours; data economy 'what could be upwards of $1 trillion in infrastructure annually' (CEO)

items.reason: Hedge lost: the CEO said the data economy is investing 'what could be' upwards of $1 trillion annually, as his own view ('I think').
items.evidence: the entirety of the data economy investing what could be upwards of $1 trillion in infrastructure annually when you put all the pieces together

items.label: Constellation Energy Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CRANE (Three Mile Island) RESTART ON TRACK FOR 2H 2027

set.signal: CRANE (Three Mile Island) RESTART ON TRACK FOR 2H 2027: the NRC approved the new-fuel licensing amendment request, clearing the path to receive new fuel, and FERC granted the waiver to TRANSFER CAPACITY INJECTION RIGHTS FROM THE EDDYSTONE facility (slated to close) TO CRANE - expected to clear many of the transmission contingencies identified in PJM's initial deliverability review so Crane can deliver full value to the grid. Fleet life extension continued with subsequent license renewal applications filed for GINNA and NINE MILE POINT 1, enabled by New York's extension of the ZEC program, leaving 'the vast majority of our power generation secured through 2050 and beyond'. Operations: 93% nuclear capacity factor and 40 TWh generated while completing SIX refueling outages (the additional planned outage days reduced the capacity factor by 1.8% compared to Q2 2025); 23-day average outage duration - outperforming the industry average duration by 40% - including a turbine upgrade at Byron Unit 1; nuclear capacity factor ran ABOVE 99% during the Mid-Atlantic heat wave before July 4

items.reason: Wording made exact: the CFO said the planned outage days reduced the capacity factor by 1.8% (not 'pts', no 'purely'), and the outage duration outperformed the industry average duration by 40%.
items.evidence: the quarter included additional planned outage days, which reduced our capacity factor by 1.8% compared to the second quarter of 2025

items.label: Constellation Energy Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: ERCOT / TEXAS read-through: the soft Texas market is

set.signal: ERCOT / TEXAS read-through: the soft Texas market is what the CEO 'fully anticipated' because BATTERY STORAGE AND OTHER SUPPLY ARE ARRIVING ON THE GRID AHEAD OF THE LOAD - 'the vast majority of the data centers that are anticipated are still at some stage of construction and not on the grid' - and Constellation/Calpine positioned accordingly; the market is expected to TIGHTEN as those data centers energize. On Governor Abbott's BATCH ZERO review, Constellation has sites in the process (plus early-mover Calpine projects that already cleared three necessary approvals and are proceeding with clients); Dave Dardis calls the governor's information requests reasonable, answerable quickly, and a TEMPORARY measure 'manageable by the industry' rather than a meaningful delay, and the CEO notes some customers' data-center water consumption is on the level of a restaurant or large store. FOUR-HOUR BATTERIES are seen as having 'a very big role', with Calpine a US leader in developing and integrating them. On new nuclear: no imminent capital commitment, but sites are being prepared (permitting, early site permits), with New York called 'a very exciting opportunity' and a template Illinois should follow

items.reason: Quoted words were not verbatim ('What we're seeing in Texas is what we fully anticipated'); the Batch Zero view was Dave Dardis', the water remark the CEO's.
items.evidence: Dave Dardis: We see this as a temporary measure here that we think is manageable by the industry

items.label: Constellation Energy Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CAPITAL ALLOCATION AND PORTFOLIO: ~$2.2B of accretive share

set.signal: PORTFOLIO AND NUCLEAR PTC: Constellation reached an agreement with LS Power to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center; following regulatory approvals and closing, the sale will satisfy the final DOJ requirement tied to the Calpine acquisition (CEO Joe Dominguez, who adds that integration with Calpine 'is progressing well'). CFO Shane Smith: following the IRS publication of the 2025 inflation adjustment (2.8%), and continuing to assume 2% inflation annually in 2026 and beyond, the projected 2030 nuclear PTC strike price will increase from $49.88 to $50.88 per MWh, which 'will increase our view of 2030 base earnings by approximately $0.30 per share' and supports the goal of sustaining double-digit base earnings growth into the 2030s.
set.figure: 2030 PTC strike price $49.88 -> $50.88/MWh; about +$0.30/share to 2030 base earnings

items.reason: Section 2 exclusions (coordinator decision): strips the share repurchases and authorization, the Brazos Valley sale price and per-kW prices, the divestiture proceeds and the buyback-driven 2029 capital-allocation sensitivity; keeps the divestiture's operating fact and the PTC update.
items.evidence: Following regulatory approvals and closing, the sale will satisfy the final DOJ requirement tied to the Calpine acquisition.
